## Summary

Filter each new release from a mixed Kinozal listing by the authoritative category marker on its own `details.php` page. The operator-owned `KINOZAL_EXCLUDED_ITEM_CATEGORIES` denylist uses readable names and group prefixes; unlisted or unknown categories fail open visibly, while denied books/music/software are stored for dedup but never reach trailer lookup or Telegram.

The previous feed-level implementation was mechanically reverted because it rejected the operator's entire `t=0` listing to remove one unwanted row. The replacement matched the updated issue plan: one shared details fetch applies item category first and the independent genre denylist second.

Closes #506

- [x] Readable group prefixes deny every descendant category
- [x] A category absent from the denylist remains deliverable regardless of numeric id

- [x] Category and genre filters share one details fetch per new item
- [x] The committed taxonomy causes no extra network request

- [x] Zero-of-N category resolution appends a pipeline error while delivery remains fail-open
- [x] Configured names absent from the taxonomy append a visible error

## Risk & Rollback

- Blast radius: new Kinozal items only, after listing extraction and dedup. Existing rows and non-Kinozal pipelines are untouched. The genre denylist keeps its independent behavior.
- Availability policy: this is a denylist, not an allowlist. Missing/ambiguous markers, new numeric ids, details failures, and stale readable names do not suppress a release; warnings and aggregate pipeline errors expose degraded classification.
- Request cost: at most one details request per new item when either denylist is configured, identical to the existing production genre-filter path; the taxonomy is committed and never fetched at runtime.
- Rollback: revert `6db0804` and `b70c565` in a PR. The earlier feed-level implementation remains reverted and must not be restored as a fallback.
- Monitoring: inspect post-filter per-item outcomes and the zero-of-N category-resolution error on the first scheduled run after the production variable is created.
